'''Paul Roesel Garabedian''' (August 2, 1927{{spaced ndash}}May 13, 2010) was a [[mathematician]] and [[numerical analysis|numerical analyst]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://cims.nyu.edu/webapps/feed/announcements |title=NYU > Courant Institute > Announcements |publisher=cims.nyu.edu |accessdate=2010-05-19 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100603051647/http://cims.nyu.edu/webapps/feed/announcements |archivedate=2010-06-03 }}</ref> Garabedian was the Director-Division of Computational Fluid Dynamics at the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]], [[New York University]].<ref>[http://www.math.nyu.edu/faculty/garabedi/ Paul Garabedian] at [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]]</ref> He is known for his contributions to the fields of [[computational fluid dynamics]] and [[plasma physics]], which ranged from elegant [[existence theorem|existence]] [[Mathematical proof|proofs]] for [[potential theory]] and [[conformal mapping]]s<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Garabedian|first1=P. R.|last2=Schiffer| first2=M.|authorlink2=Menahem Max Schiffer| title=On existence theorems of potential theory and conformal mapping|jstor=1969517|journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]]|doi=10.2307/1969517|year=1950|volume=52|number=1|pages=164–187}}</ref> to the design and optimization of [[stellarator]]s.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?nom_unit=Plasma%20Physics%20(DPP)&year=2004 |title=Archive (1995-present)|publisher=[[American Physical Society]]|accessdate=2009-04-29}}</ref> Garabedian was elected a member of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]] in 1975.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nasonline.org/site/Dir/818102646?pg=vprof&mbr=1002868&returl=http://www.nasonline.org/site/Dir/818102646?pg=srch&view=basic&retmk=search_again_link|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604030806/http://www.nasonline.org/site/Dir/818102646?pg=vprof&mbr=1002868&returl=http:%2F%2Fwww.nasonline.org%2Fsite%2FDir%2F818102646%3Fpg=srch&view=basic&retmk=search_again_link|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 4, 2011|title=National Academy of Sciences|publisher=[[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]]|accessdate=2009-10-31}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Born in  [[Cincinnati]], [[Ohio]], Garabedian received a bachelor's degree from [[Brown University]] in 1946 and a master's degree from the [[Harvard University]] in 1947, both in mathematics. He received his Ph.D., also from Harvard University, in 1948 under the direction of [[Lars Ahlfors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/news/in-memory/in-memory|title=In Memory Of ...|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|accessdate=26 June 2010}}</ref> It was at Brown University that he met his longtime colleague and collaborator, [[Frances Bauer]].<ref>[http://history.siam.org/oralhistories/garabedian.htm Interview with Paul Garabedian]</ref>

In 1949 Garabedian joined the faculty at the [[University of California]] as an Assistant Professor and became associate professor in 1952. In 1956, he moved to [[Stanford University]] as a professor of mathematics. In 1959 he moved to the Institute of Mathematical Sciences [later renamed the Courant Institute] at New York University. In 1978 he was appointed the Director-Division of [[Computational Fluid Dynamics]] at the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]], New York University. In a long and fruitful academic career, Garabedian supervised 27 Ph.D. theses.  The first was in 1953 (Edward McLeod) and the last came in 1997 (Connie Chen).

==Honors and awards==
*[[Sloan Fellowship]], 1961–63
*[[Guggenheim Fellowship]], 1966<ref>[http://www.gf.org/fellows/5088-paul-roesel-garabedian Paul Roesel Garabedian – John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110603234814/http://www.gf.org/fellows/5088-paul-roesel-garabedian |date=2011-06-03 }}</ref>
*Fairchild Distinguished Scholar [[Caltech]], 1975
*NASA Public Service Group Achievement Award by [[Langley Research Center|NASA Langley Research Center]], 1976
*[[Boris Pregel]] Award, [[New York Academy of Sciences]], 1980
*[[Birkhoff Prize]] of the [[American Mathematical Society|AMS]] and [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|SIAM]], 1983<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/prizes/birkhoff-prize.html|title=George David Birkhoff Prize in Applied Mathematics|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|accessdate=2009-11-02}}</ref>
*[[Theodore von Kármán Prize]], [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|SIAM]], 1989

*''Supercritical Wing Sections II'', with F. Bauer, [[David Korn (computer scientist)|D. Korn]] and [[Antony Jameson|A. Jameson]]. ''Lecture Notes in Economics and Mathematical Systems'', Springer-Verlag (1975), {{ISBN|0-387-07029-X}}.<ref>[https://ntrs.nasa.gov/search.jsp?R=816614&id=4&as=false&or=false&qs=Ns%3DHarvestDate%257c1%26N%3D4294902518 Abstract of ''Supercritical Wing Sections II'']</ref>
